title: Email-verification token is not bound to the email address: a stale link verifies a newly changed, never-proven email
description: EmailVerificationTokenGenerator._make_hash_value signs only user.pk + user.password + timestamp + profile.email_verified — user.email is absent. An authenticated user can PATCH /api/user/me/ to change user.email; UpdateUserQuery resets email_verified only when it was previously True, so a token issued while verified=False keeps identical hash inputs after the change. VerifyEmailQuery then sets email_verified=True for the new, never-proven address. StoreViewSet.create (viewset.py:463-469) treats that flag as the mailbox-control attestation for claiming a public store, while phone remains a separate requirement.
root_cause: _make_hash_value (services/services.py:202-209) omits user.email from the signed material, so the token proves only 'this user requested verification at time T', not 'this specific address was proven'.
intended_behavior: email_verified must attest control of the CURRENT user.email; changing the address must invalidate outstanding verification tokens (include the email — or a hash of it — in the token value).

trace.description: PATCH /api/user/me/ with UserUpdateSerializer {email} reaches the self-scoped update and calls UpdateUserQuery.
email change resets profile.email_verified only when it was True; when already False, no hash input changes.
GET /api/verify-email/?uid=&token= is AllowAny and calls VerifyEmailQuery.
after check_token succeeds, profile.email_verified=True is persisted for the account's current user.email.

evidence.description: _make_hash_value returns pk+password+timestamp+verified; user.email absent. The inherited _make_token_with_timestamp signs only this hash value.
UpdateUserQuery changes user.email; profile.email_verified is reset only inside `if profile.email_verified`, so an already-False flag leaves every token hash input unchanged.
UserUpdateSerializer exposes only email and UserUpdateMethod calls UpdateUserQuery; UserViewSetConfig.update is IsAuthenticated and self-scoped (viewset_config.py:36-41).
validate_email only rejects iexact duplicates on other auth.User rows; any unused address is accepted.
RegisterUserSerializer declares required confirm_password; the shared validate() rejects a missing or mismatched confirmation.
SendVerificationEmailQuery creates uid+token with email_verification_token, builds the /api/verify-email/ link, and _send_branded_mail sends it to user.email.
send_verification_email reloads the User and calls SendVerificationEmailQuery; registration enqueues it post-commit (services.py:169) and resend uses the same task (auth_views.py:424).
VerifyEmailView.get is AllowAny and passes uid/token to VerifyEmailQuery.
router.register(r'user', UserViewSet) exposes the detail route used as /api/user/me/; the configured queryset is self-scoped rather than lookup-scoped.
StoreViewSet.create requires profile.email_verified (and phone) — the forged flag satisfies the anti-abuse email gate.

conditions.description: Any registered user with a valid access token; registration is open and the email update is self-scoped.

Target email must be unregistered on auth.User (iexact uniqueness); profile.email_verified must be False when the token is generated and False after the email change — already False, or reset from True by UpdateUserQuery.

Token use must occur within EmailVerificationTokenGenerator.timeout=86400 of token generation; receive the controlled-address verification mail before changing email because the queued sender uses the address current when it runs.

execution.attacker_perspective: Authenticated platform user wanting to forge the verified-email attestation for an address they do not control.
payloads: POST /api/register/ {username:'attacker', email:'attacker@mail.com', password:'<strong-password>', confirm_password:'<strong-password>', phone:'+5491100000002', accept_terms:true}
GET /api/verify-email/?uid=<uid from verification email>&token=<token from verification email>
instructions: 1. Register an account with an email the attacker controls; wait for the verification email at that controlled address and extract uid/token T while profile.email_verified=False. Do not change email before that mail is generated/sent: the Celery task reloads the user and sends to whatever user.email is current.
2. Log in and send PATCH /api/user/me/ {email:'victim@example.com'} with the Bearer access token; the serializer accepts any iexact-unused address and UpdateUserQuery leaves email_verified False.
3. GET /api/verify-email/?uid=<uid>&token=T — check_token recomputes the identical hash (pk, password, timestamp, verified all unchanged) and VerifyEmailQuery sets email_verified=True.
4. The account now carries victim@example.com with email_verified=True — an attestation the mailbox owner never made; store creation's email gate is satisfied (phone anchor still required).
execution.observed_result: Source-traced: _make_hash_value omits user.email so the pre-change token validates post-change; VerifyEmailQuery sets the flag on check_token success; StoreViewSet.create then treats the unproven address as verified for the claim gate.

remediation.strategy: Bind the verification token to the address it was issued for: include user.email (or an HMAC of it) in EmailVerificationTokenGenerator._make_hash_value so any email change invalidates outstanding links; alternatively persist the address the mail was sent to and compare it at verification time.

likelihood.reason: Trivially executable by any registered user within the 24h window; requires only reading one's own verification mail and two API calls.

impact.reason: Forges the email_verified attestation for an unproven address — defeats the store-claim anti-abuse email gate (phone anchor still required) and points account mail at an address the owner never authorized; no direct data exposure or account takeover.

confidence.reason: Hash inputs, the self-scoped /api/user/me/ update path, serializer uniqueness and required register fields, queued token issuance, verify-email route/view, token timeout, and the store-claim consumer were verified line-by-line; the sequence is deterministic once the controlled-address verification mail is received.
